outcome: admission to neonatal intensive care unit
cohort: 3677 women who gave birth between 2012-2016, excluding those with intrauterine fetal death, birthweight below the 10th percentile, and antepartum cesarean delivery for any indication
finding: Isolated fetal microcephaly in term fetuses is not advantageous for a vaginal delivery and does not pose a greater risk of adverse perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of vaginal operative deliveries between the group with isolated fetal microcephaly and the control group, and the study group had no intrapartum cesarean deliveries compared to 6.3% of the reference group.
birth_weight: Neonates in the microcephaly group were smaller (3323.2 ± 432.2 vs. 2957.0 ± 330.4 g, p < .001), with lower birthweight percentile (60.5 ± 26.5 vs. 33.6 ± 21.5%, p < .001)
